Prevention: Always use healthy and uninfested seed tubers for planting.
Always store seed tubers in cool conditions in storage before planting.
Earth-up to prevent tuber exposure during growing period.
Regularly irrigate the field to prevent cracking in soil (the pest often resides in cracks and crevices).
Store healthy looking tubers away from infested and/or bruised tubers.
Harvest entire potato crop immediately, when mature; do not leave potato tubers in the field after harvest.
Do not leave harvested tubers over-night in the field.
Store harvested tubers in cool, dry places in a facility with doors and windows covered with a net.
Monitoring: Once a week check the leaves and stems of 25 randomly selected plants/ropani.
Look for mines across the leaves, and weak stems.
Use pheromone traps at 1 trap/ ropani, to monitor adult moths (males).
Consider action when there are 20 or more adult moths in a trap per night.
Direct Control: When tubers are stored, apply shade dried
Chenopodium botrytis is being used as a repellent, chop and place 300-330g per 8kg potato in a crate.
Put 1 layer of this botanical above and below the stored tubers.
When tubers are stored, apply dust of
Acharus calamus sweet flag (Bojho) @1.5-2 g/kg over the stored tubers and over the surface of the gunny bags.
Bacillus thuringiensis on crop foliages in the field during late afternoon, at 1g/l water, spray at 25 l/ropani.
